cards.text: The writer of Hebrews has been telling believers one thing, LOUD and clear: God's Son is far greater than the angels. He just warned them not to drift away, and friend, I once drifted all the way to the back of a junk drawer, so I'm LISTENING. Now he talks about the world to come, the one he's been writing about.

cards.question: The writer says God has put the world to come under the angels.

cards.text: Then he quotes Scripture that asks God a question: “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?” Great question. Some of us asked something like it from the bottom of a junk drawer.
The quote keeps going: God made man a little lower than the angels and crowned him with glory and honor. Man gets a CROWN, and all I ever got was my name carved into my handle!

cards.question: In that quote, God crowns man with glory and honor. How much does He put under man's feet?

cards.text: The writer says that when God put all things under man, He left nothing outside his control. Then he takes a look around at how things are right now.

cards.question: The writer says that right now we can see everything under man's control.

cards.text: Everything under man's feet, and I've watched people lose a wrestling match to a fitted sheet. But the writer says we DO see Jesus, made a little lower than the angels and now crowned with glory and honor.

cards.question: The writer gives a reason Jesus is now crowned with glory and honor. What is it?
By the grace of God, Jesus tasted death for ___.

cards.text: Now the writer says God is bringing many sons to glory, and Jesus is the author of their salvation. And it was fitting for God to make Him perfect in one very particular way.

cards.question: How was it fitting for God to make Jesus, the author of their salvation, perfect?

cards.text: Now the writer looks at Jesus, the One who sanctifies, and at the people He sanctifies. Here comes the part that hits home, baker.

cards.question: The writer says the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family.
Because they're one family, Jesus is not ashamed to call them ___.

cards.text: Friend, I've seen people hide behind a pillar at the airport to dodge their own cousin, but Jesus is NOT ashamed to call them brothers. Then the writer quotes three lines as Jesus' own words, starting with this one.

cards.question: In the first line, who does Jesus say He will proclaim God's name to?

cards.text: Jesus also says, “I will sing Your praises in the assembly.” Then come the other two lines: “I will put My trust in Him.” and “Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”
Now, since the children have flesh and blood, Jesus shared in their humanity too. And the writer says exactly why.

cards.question: By His death, Jesus would destroy the one who holds the power of death, the ___.
Jesus also came to free people who were held in slavery all their lives. What were they slaves to?

cards.text: Back in the junk drawer, we held our breath every time it opened, which is IMPRESSIVE for a bunch of stuff with no lungs. So believe me, I know what it's like to live scared.

cards.question: The writer says it's the angels that Jesus helps.

cards.text: Not angels. He helps the descendants of Abraham, so He had to be made like His brothers in every way, to serve God and make atonement for the sins of the people.

cards.question: Being made like His brothers, Jesus could become a merciful and faithful ___ ___ in service to God.

cards.text: One more thing, baker, and it's a BIG one. Jesus Himself suffered when He was tempted.

cards.question: Because Jesus suffered when He was tempted, who is He able to help?

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says he 'drifted all the way to the back of a junk drawer.' In his backstory he didn't drift. He was picked up, carried across the kitchen and slid into the drawer. The joke changes his backstory, and the comparison doesn't match the core action of Hebrews 2:1, which is drifting away from what was heard.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote sentence, 'Great question.' and the junk drawer line. It isn't the opening card, so it is limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says, 'I've seen people hide behind a pillar at the airport to dodge their own cousin.' His only world is the Millers' kitchen, the junk drawer and the Dorinverse, so he has never been to an airport. The joke adds a new experience to his backstory. It could be reworded as a general observation instead.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The blank follows 'the,' so 'the devil' reads naturally but 'the Goliath' doesn't, and 'the Pharaoh' is awkward. The grammar makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card is only a junk drawer joke and a reflection on verse 15, which card 9 already covered. It tells no part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Abraham is named here for the first time in the walkthrough ('the descendants of Abraham'), but Papa Dorin doesn't say simply who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This is a 'who' question, but the wrong answers aren't real details from the Bible, and they aren't believable. 'Those who never struggle' wouldn't need help at all. The right answer also stands out because it repeats 'tempted' from the question.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.
